candidates.title: Rethinking functional mobility within contemporary physical activity guidelines: a commentary.
candidates.abstract: Regular physical activity promotes health, prevents chronic disease, and supports healthy aging, yet current physical activity recommendations primarily emphasize movement behavior rather than the capacities that enable safe and effective participation. In this Commentary, we propose functional mobility as a proposed movement-capacity construct that complements the behavioral focus of physical activity by integrating joint mobility, muscular strength and power, balance and postural control, coordination, motor control, cardiorespiratory endurance, and movement adaptability. We distinguish functional mobility from physical activity, physical fitness, physical function, functional performance, and intrinsic capacity while recognizing their reciprocal relationships. Building on the World Health Organization's International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health and Healthy Ageing frameworks, we present a noncausal, heuristic model in which functional mobility connects movement behavior with functional performance and healthy aging. We discuss implications for clinical practice, rehabilitation, and public health without proposing that this framework replace current physical activity recommendations. Research priorities include reaching consensus on the construct's definition, developing multidimensional assessment approaches, validating the construct across diverse populations, and evaluating interventions. Considering both how much individuals move and their capacity to meet everyday movement demands may broaden the study of movement health and inform efforts to preserve participation, independence, and quality of life across the lifespan.

candidates.title: Hypercalcemia-Associated Renal Salt Wasting Presenting With Hypovolemic Hyponatremia: A Case Report.
candidates.abstract: Hyponatremia is a common electrolyte disorder defined as a serum sodium level below 135 mmol/L. However, its occurrence in association with hypercalcemia and renal sodium wasting remains a rare clinical phenomenon. We present the case of a 56-year-old male with a history of laryngeal cancer who developed moderate, persistent hypovolemic hyponatremia following extensive neck surgery, including a total thyroidectomy. Despite receiving standard enteral nutrition and free water flushes, the patient exhibited distinct clinical signs of extracellular volume depletion, including poor skin turgor, polyuria, hypotension, tachycardia, and a low serum osmolality of 263 mOsm/kg. Common causes of hyponatremia, such as the syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion (SIADH), pseudohyponatremia, and adrenal insufficiency, were systematically excluded. A normal saline challenge elicited an increase in serum sodium alongside a notable decrease in both urine sodium and urine osmolality. This response supported a volume-responsive component but was not considered independently diagnostic of renal salt wasting or sufficient to exclude SIADH. Other common causes of hyponatremia were evaluated, and the overall clinical picture suggested renal sodium loss in the setting of concurrent hypercalcemia as a potential contributing mechanism. Hypercalcemia may alter renal sodium and water handling through calcium-sensing receptor-mediated effects on tubular transport and impairment of urinary concentrating ability. In this patient, these effects, together with extracellular volume depletion and ongoing enteral free-water administration, may have contributed to the development and persistence of hypotonic hyponatremia. Volume repletion was followed by resolution of polyuria and normalization of serum sodium and calcium. This case highlights hypercalcemia-associated renal tubular dysfunction as a potential and underrecognized contributor to hypovolemic hyponatremia. Recognition of the patient's volume status and the multifactorial nature of the disorder is important to avoid inappropriate fluid restriction.

candidates.title: Vertebral fractures unmasking Cushing disease: an unexpected argument for secondary osteoporosis screening.
candidates.abstract: Osteoporosis poses a substantial health and financial burden. Although secondary causes are more common in men, they are screened less for osteoporosis than their female counterparts. We present the case of a 70-year-old man with a history of an adrenal incidentaloma with a recent diagnosis of 2 vertebral fractures. Initial workup revealed adrenocorticotropic hormone-dependent hypercortisolism. Imaging confirmed a pituitary macroadenoma, suggestive of Cushing disease (CD). Lifestyle modifications, calcium and vitamin D supplementation, and intravenous zoledronic acid were initiated to treat the severe osteoporosis. Pituitary surgery was carried out, with pathology revealing a Crooke cell adenoma. This case illustrates the importance of screening for osteoporosis in men, including thorough evaluation to rule out secondary causes. Moreover, a critical evaluation of the current approach to bone health in CD is provided.

candidates.title: Pituitary Stalk Interruption Syndrome Presenting as Primary Amenorrhea: Magnetic Resonance Imaging Demonstration of the Characteristic Diagnostic Triad.
candidates.abstract: Pituitary stalk interruption syndrome (PSIS) is a rare congenital pituitary malformation characterized by the triad of anterior pituitary hypoplasia, an absent or interrupted pituitary stalk, and an ectopic posterior pituitary. We report the case of a 21-year-old woman who presented with primary amenorrhea and poorly developed secondary sexual characteristics. Hormonal evaluation revealed central hypothyroidism, markedly reduced morning serum cortisol, and suppressed gonadotropin levels, indicating hypopituitarism with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism. Pelvic ultrasonography demonstrated a markedly hypoplastic uterus and bilaterally small ovaries. Magnetic resonance imaging of the sellar region revealed a hypoplastic anterior pituitary gland, nonvisualization of the pituitary stalk, and an ectopic posterior pituitary bright spot at the median eminence beneath the optic chiasm. These characteristic imaging findings established the diagnosis of PSIS. This case highlights the importance of considering PSIS in women presenting with primary amenorrhea and delayed pubertal development. Recognition of the characteristic magnetic resonance imaging triad facilitates timely endocrine evaluation, hormone replacement therapy, and long-term follow-up. RésuméLe syndrome d’interruption de la tige pituitaire (SITP) est une malformation congénitale rare de l’hypophyse, caractérisée par une triade associant une hypoplasie de l’antéhypophyse, une absence ou une interruption de la tige pituitaire et une neurohypophyse ectopique. Nous rapportons le cas d’une femme de 21 ans consultant pour une aménorrhée primaire et un développement insuffisant des caractères sexuels secondaires. Le bilan hormonal a révélé une hypothyroïdie centrale, une diminution marquée du cortisol sérique matinal et une suppression des taux de gonadotrophines, en faveur d’un hypopituitarisme associé à un hypogonadisme hypogonadotrope. L’échographie pelvienne a montré un utérus très hypoplasique et des ovaires bilatéralement de petite taille. L’imagerie par résonance magnétique (IRM) de la région sellaire a mis en évidence une hypoplasie de l’antéhypophyse, une absence de visualisation de la tige pituitaire et un hypersignal spontané T1 ectopique de la neurohypophyse au niveau de l’éminence médiane, sous le chiasma optique. Ces signes radiologiques caractéristiques ont permis d’établir le diagnostic de SITP. Ce cas souligne l’importance d’évoquer le SITP chez les femmes présentant une aménorrhée primaire et un retard du développement pubertaire. La reconnaissance de la triade caractéristique à l’IRM permet une évaluation endocrinienne précoce, l’instauration d’un traitement hormonal substitutif et un suivi à long terme.

candidates.title: Successful treatment of symptomatic locally recurrent unresectable pheochromocytoma with percutaneous ablations.
candidates.abstract: Metastatic or locally recurrent pheochromocytomas (PCCs) present significant therapeutic challenges, particularly in patients with symptomatic or progressive disease. Current treatment options, apart from surgery, are predominantly palliative. Minimally invasive percutaneous ablative techniques have emerged as promising treatment modalities for selected patients with unresectable or metastatic PCCs. We report a case of a woman with neurofibromatosis type 1 with a symptomatic, progressive unresectable 3.3 cm PCC recurrence in the adrenal bed following 2 prior surgical resections. Three consecutive percutaneous ablations-2 cryoablations followed by irreversible electroporation led to clinical, biochemical, and radiographic resolution of the disease. Preprocedural medical management with terazosin, metyrosine, and atenolol was essential in ensuring the safety of the interventions. The patient demonstrated sustained local and biochemical disease control at 4 years of follow-up. This case illustrates the effectiveness of repeated ablative therapies in achieving sustained remission in unresectable recurrent PCC and emphasizes the importance of multidisciplinary care.

candidates.title: Giant adrenal teratoma mimicking renal angiomyolipoma during pregnancy with coexisting fetal pulmonary sequestration: a case report.
candidates.abstract: Adrenal tumors during pregnancy are rare, but their detection is increasing due to prenatal imaging. Retroperitoneal fat-containing tumors, such as mature teratomas, can easily mimic renal angiomyolipoma (RAML), especially when the gravid uterus displaces anatomical landmarks. Excluding functional tumors (e.g., pheochromocytoma) is critical to prevent lethal hypertensive crises and guide multidisciplinary team (MDT) management. A 31-year-old primigravida (12 weeks' gestation) presented with a 9.8 × 13.3 × 10.9 cm fat-containing right retroperitoneal mass on MRI, mimicking renal angiomyolipoma or teratoma. Concurrently, fetal ultrasound at 22 + 4 weeks identified an incidental left-sided fetal pulmonary sequestration. Normal catecholamine and cortisol levels confirmed a non-functional tumor, warranting a multidisciplinary team (MDT) strategy of watchful waiting. The patient successfully delivered a live infant via elective cesarean section at 37 + 1 weeks. Postpartum, she underwent elective laparoscopic resection of the retroperitoneal tumor. Intraoperatively, the massive tumor encased the inferior vena cava (IVC) and right renal vein with dense adhesions. A laceration occurred on the posterior wall of the IVC during dissection, which was successfully repaired using vascular sutures without significant blood loss (200 mL). Postoperative pathology confirmed a mature adrenal teratoma. Both mother and neonate showed excellent outcomes during follow-up. This case highlights the diagnostic challenge of differentiating giant fat-containing retroperitoneal tumors during pregnancy. For non-functional retroperitoneal tumors without signs of malignancy, delaying surgery until the postpartum period is a safe strategy. In cases involving major vascular encasement, the surgical team must be fully prepared to manage unexpected vascular injuries. A multidisciplinary approach is highly recommended to optimize outcomes for rare maternal tumors and incidental fetal anomalies.

candidates.title: Hand and finger symptoms in older adults: a clinical audit of detection and management gaps in Danish general practice.
candidates.abstract: Hand osteoarthritis (OA) is common among older adults. Recommendations support a combination of non-pharmacological and pharmacological treatments. However, real-world data on prevalence and treatment patterns in primary care are lacking. To investigate the prevalence and characteristics of hand and finger pain/swelling among elderly patients presenting to general practice, and to audit the quality and comprehensiveness of their clinical management against evidence-based recommendations. We conducted a four-week clinical audit of all consecutive patients ≥70 years of age attending general practices in Denmark with recording of current symptoms and signs characteristic of hand OA as well as prior related diagnostic investigations and treatments. The study included 348 patients from 16 general practices, with 42% (n = 147) experiencing hand/or finger pain/swelling. Pain during usage (64%, n = 95) and stiffness (39%, n = 57) were the most common symptoms. Clinical findings suggestive of hand OA were present in 61% (n = 90) of symptomatic patients, with 41% (n = 60) reporting reduced activities of daily living. Only 50% (n = 73) of symptomatic patients had previously consulted their GP about these symptoms, and referral rates to specialists and allied health professionals were low. Management strategies were limited, with 33% (n = 49) using analgesics and 7.5% (n = 11) using assistive devices. Hand and finger symptoms are prevalent among older adults in general practice, with significant functional impact. Management patterns displayed low referral rates to allied healthcare professionals and limited use of non-pharmacological interventions. Further research is needed to understand patient preferences and barriers to accessing recommended care.
candidates.journal: Scandinavian journal of primary health care

candidates.title: Multidisciplinary Approach to Functioning Pituitary Neuroendocrine Tumors.
candidates.abstract: Functioning pituitary neuroendocrine tumors require individualized multidisciplinary management because of both tumor mass effects and hormone hypersecretion. Evaluation includes biochemical assessment of hormone excess, pituitary imaging, visual and cranial nerve examination, and assessment of comorbidities. Surgical resection, most commonly via an endoscopic endonasal transsphenoidal approach, is the primary treatment for most functioning tumors. However, prolactinomas are generally treated with dopamine agonists, whereas surgery is typically first-line for growth hormone-, adrenocorticotropic hormone-, and thyroid-stimulating hormone-secreting tumors. Persistent or recurrent disease may require repeat surgery, medical therapy, or radiation.

candidates.title: Examining the relationship between objective and patient-reported physical function in adults with cancer.
candidates.abstract: Cancer and its therapies negatively impact physical function (PF), which is commonly captured using patient-reported PF measures. Though important, patient-report PF tools may fail to capture important aspects of objectively measured PF, limiting their ability to provide a comprehensive assessment of PF. This study aimed to compare patient-reported (PROMIS-Physical Function Computer Adaptive Test, PROMIS PF) and objective (Bellarmine Norton Assessment Tool, BNAT) measures of PF in adults with a history of cancer. This cross-sectional study included a referred and volunteer sample of 94 adults with a history of cancer (91.5% women, 60.1 ± 10.8 years) who completed the BNAT and the PROMIS PF. The BNAT includes the 2-minute step test (MST), 30-second sit-to-stand (STS), 30-second arm curl, and timed-up-and-go (TUG), with total scores calculated from the sum of subscale scores. Pearson's correlations, variance (r2), and descriptive statistics were used to evaluate the relationships between BNAT and PROMIS scores. Weak correlations were observed between PROMIS PF total scores and BNAT total scores (r = 0.313, p = 0.002) and between the PROMIS PF and BNAT raw scores, including STS (r = 0.362, p = 0.001), arm curl (r = 0.320, p = 0.002), and TUG (r = -0.319, p = 0.002). Variance explained ranged from 3.3%-13.1%, suggesting limited overlap between subjective and objective measures. Our findings suggest that patient-reported and performance-based assessments of PF are generally weakly associated in adults with a history of cancer. These findings highlight the potential value of incorporating both approaches to provide a more comprehensive understanding of PF in clinical and research settings. NCT06039488.

candidates.title: Pituitary residual tumor detection: incremental value of multimodal assessment.
candidates.abstract: Postoperative residual tumor is associated with regrowth and recurrence in pituitary adenomas, making maximal safe resection an important therapeutic goal. We evaluated the incremental contribution of microscopy, endoscopic inspection, and 3.0-T intraoperative magnetic resonance imaging (iMRI) to residual tumor detection and assessment of the planned extent of resection. In this retrospective single-center cohort study, 120 consecutive eligible patients undergoing transsphenoidal surgery for pituitary adenoma underwent sequential microsurgical resection, endoscopic inspection, and iMRI. Initial endoscopic inspection confirmed the planned extent of resection in 95/120 patients (79.2%) and indicated further resection in 25/120 (20.8%). After any indicated further resection, repeat endoscopic inspection confirmed planned extent of resection achievement before iMRI in all 120 patients. At iMRI, planned extent of resection was judged achieved in 85/120 patients (70.8%), whereas residual tumor was suspected in 35/120 (29.2%) before any iMRI-triggered resection. Among 95 patients considered complete at initial endoscopic inspection, iMRI identified suspected residual tumor in 21 (22.1%). Escalation beyond microscopy was more frequent in recurrent than primary adenomas (12/14, 85.7% vs 34/106, 32.1%; p < 0.001). Each doubling of preoperative tumor volume was associated with higher odds of iMRI-suspected residual tumor (OR 1.79, 95% CI 1.32-2.44; p < 0.001). Sequential endoscopic inspection and iMRI provided complementary information beyond microsurgical assessment. Additional assessment was more frequently required in recurrent adenomas, while increasing preoperative tumor volume was associated with iMRI-suspected residual tumor. These findings support prospective evaluation of risk-adapted multimodal intraoperative assessment.

candidates.title: Subarachnoid Pneumocephalus Following Endoscopic Transsphenoidal Surgery.
candidates.abstract: A 26-year-old man with past medical history of prolactinoma presented two weeks status post endoscopic transsphenoid prolactinoma excision with a positional headache and cerebrospinal fluid rhinorrhea; he was found to have diffuse subarachnoid air. There are few reports of subarachnoid pneumocephalus in the emergency medicine literature. Pneumocephalus, particularly tension pneumocephalus, typically occurs in the setting of traumatic skull fractures. However, emergency physicians should be aware of subarachnoid pneumocephalus in the setting of endoscopic skull base surgeries.
candidates.journal: Clinical practice and cases in emergency medicine

candidates.title: Contemporary Management of Adrenal Tumors.
candidates.abstract: Background/Objectives: Widespread use of high-resolution cross-sectional imaging has made the incidentally discovered adrenal mass a common clinical problem. Although most adrenal incidentalomas are non-functioning benign adenomas, clinicians must distinguish them from actionable pathology such as functional adenomas, adrenocortical carcinoma, and pheochromocytoma. This review outlines the contemporary diagnostic algorithm for adrenal incidentalomas and the main indications for surgical and medical intervention. Methods: We performed a narrative review of current society guidelines and of the primary literature underlying their recommendations on anatomic, biochemical, and surgical evaluation, comparing recommendations and evidence grades where guidelines differ. Results: Management is driven primarily by imaging phenotype, lesion size, and hormonal function. Unenhanced computed tomography attenuation ≤ 10 Hounsfield units is highly specific for a benign lipid-rich adenoma. Hormonal evaluation should exclude hypercortisolism in all patients and pheochromocytoma in all but asymptomatic patients with homogeneous, lipid-rich lesions, with testing for primary aldosteronism and androgen excess when clinically indicated. Minimally invasive adrenalectomy is standard for hormonally active benign adenomas and most pheochromocytomas, whereas open adrenalectomy remains preferred for suspected adrenocortical carcinoma that is large or locally invasive, to avoid tumor capsule rupture. Novel therapies, including peptide receptor radionuclide therapy, show efficacy in advanced disease. Conclusions: Society guidelines agree on most of the diagnostic pathway but diverge on surveillance of large benign lesions, interpretation of cortisol testing, and the surgical approach to suspected carcinoma. A standardized, multidisciplinary approach that recognizes these differences and the strength of the underlying evidence optimizes outcomes while preventing unnecessary procedures.

candidates.title: Atrial Leadless Pacing in Combination with Existing ICD Systems in Long QT Syndrome.
candidates.abstract: Long QT syndrome is an inherited or acquired condition characterized by prolonged ventricular repolarization and is characterized by a propensity for life-threatening ventricular arrhythmias. Management often incorporates beta blockers, which have the greatest effect on reducing arrhythmic risk, and implantable cardiac defibrillator (ICD) implantation. Subcutaneous ICDs provide effective defibrillation therapy while avoiding intravascular leads and are an attractive option for patients at high risk of infection or thrombosis, or for younger patients to reduce intravascular lead dwell time. Subcutaneous ICDs provide defibrillation therapy but do not offer pacing and antitachycardia pacing. Leadless pacemakers are often favored for similar reasons, and combined use with ICDs introduces challenges, including device interaction. We report 2 cases of interaction between ICD sensing and atrial leadless pacemakers in long QT syndrome, including a case of S-ICD oversensing, not yet described in the literature, and a comparative case in a transvenous system.

candidates.title: Acute diencephalic syndrome after transventricular resection of giant pituitary adenomas with third ventricular extension: clinical course and association with extent of resection.
candidates.abstract: To describe acute diencephalic syndrome (ADS) after superior transventricular surgery for giant pituitary adenomas with true third-ventricular extension, and to explore the association of ADS with extent of resection in a selected cohort. We retrospectively analyzed 40 adults operated on in 2015-2025 (23 total, 17 subtotal resections; 22 anterior transcallosal and 18 transcortical transventricular approaches). Postoperative AVP-D was distinguished from multidomain ADS, graded retrospectively according to the previously published four-stage framework. Final-stage agreement was reassessed independently in all 40 patients. Postoperative AVP-D occurred in all 40 patients; four had isolated AVP-D without ADS. ADS occurred in 36/40 (90.0%): 23/23 after total and 13/17 after subtotal resection (risk difference 23.5 percentage points; 95% Newcombe CI 3.5-47.3; two-sided Fisher exact p = 0.026). Stage III-IV ADS occurred in 9/23 versus 3/17 (p = 0.179). Independent final-stage agreement was 36/40 (90.0%; linear-weighted κ = 0.926). Five patients required mechanical ventilation, and two died. ADS was frequent in this anatomically selected transventricular cohort, but the operational definition is not specific for hypothalamic injury and the observational comparison is vulnerable to confounding by indication. The observed lower ADS frequency after subtotal resection is hypothesis-generating. Prospective multicenter validation is necessary.

candidates.title: Pituitary Neuroendocrine Tumors in the Pediatric Population.
candidates.abstract: Pediatric pituitary neuroendocrine tumors (PPitNETs) are rare but present significant clinical challenges in children. Their diverse presentations necessitate comprehensive endocrinologic and radiographic evaluation. They are most commonly prolactin-secreting or adrenocorticotropic hormone-secreting. A genetic mutation can be present, particularly in young patients with aggressive disease. Management is multidisciplinary. Medical therapy is first-line treatment of prolactinomas, and surgery is first-line treatment of most other PPitNETs, with reasonable remission rates when performed in experienced centers. Long-term outcomes are favorable, although hypopituitarism and lifelong hormone replacement remain important concerns. Ongoing surveillance is essential to ensure detect recurrence, and monitor treatment-related complications.

candidates.title: An Anatomy-Based Clinical Decision Framework for Precision Radiation Therapy of Peri-Optic Sellar and Parasellar Tumors.
candidates.abstract: In peri-optic sellar and parasellar tumors, visual preservation requires protection from both radiation injury and progression of inadequately controlled disease. This structured narrative review synthesizes guidelines, systematic reviews, and clinical cohorts identified through targeted PubMed/MEDLINE searches updated through 22 August 2026, covering pituitary neuroendocrine tumors, craniopharyngiomas, and meningiomas. Predominantly retrospective evidence and inconsistent functional reporting limit comparisons between radiation modalities. We propose an anatomy-based framework integrating therapeutic intent, tumor-optic geometry, achievable target coverage, anatomical stability, prior treatment, and baseline visual and endocrine function. Minimum tumor-optic distance alone is insufficient for modality selection. Single-fraction stereotactic radiosurgery is suited to compact, stable targets when disease-specific coverage is achievable within organ-at-risk limits. Hypofractionated stereotactic radiotherapy in three to five fractions may address focal peri-optic dose conflicts, whereas conventionally fractionated precision radiotherapy may accommodate broad contact, complex geometry, or dynamic cystic disease. Automated perimetry, optical coherence tomography, and axis-specific endocrine assessment support longitudinal surveillance; isolated retinal thinning does not establish radiation-induced optic neuropathy. New functional deficits require assessment of tumor status, treatment chronology, spatial dose, and competing causes. The proposed framework requires prospective validation and provides a practical basis for multidisciplinary decisions that jointly evaluate durable tumor control and long-term functional preservation.

candidates.title: Endocrinopathies in Inherited Leukodystrophies: A Scoping Review of Reported Frequencies, Diagnostic Strategies, and Treatment.
candidates.abstract: Leukodystrophies are a diverse group of inherited disorders affecting central nervous system white matter, with onset from infancy to adulthood. Although neurological symptoms dominate, endocrine dysfunctions are increasingly recognized as significant contributors to disease course. These can arise directly from genetic mutations or secondarily due to hypothalamic-pituitary or peripheral gland involvement. This scoping review focuses on leukodystrophies associated with hormonal abnormalities, summarizing current diagnostic approaches, preventive strategies, and treatment options. Literature from PubMed/MEDLINE and Embase (1991-May 2026) was analysed, including original research, reviews, meta-analyses, and case reports. Endocrinopathies commonly observed include adrenal insufficiency, hypogonadism, growth hormone deficiency, hypothyroidism, and diabetes mellitus. Disorders such as X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy, POLR3-related leukodystrophy, vanishing white matter disease, and Aicardi-Goutières syndrome show distinct hormonal involvement patterns. Early detection and timely hormone replacement can improve growth, development, metabolic stability, and quality of life, while preventing severe complications. Diagnosis integrates clinical evaluation, hormonal testing, neuroimaging, and advanced molecular analyses, including whole-exome or whole-genome sequencing. Effective management requires a multidisciplinary approach combining supportive care, endocrine replacement, and selected disease-modifying therapies. Understanding the interplay between neurological and endocrine features is crucial for optimizing care and improving long-term outcomes.

candidates.title: Long-term metabolic and biochemical outcomes of pasireotide LAR in resistant acromegaly.
candidates.abstract: Pasireotide long‑acting release (PAS‑LAR) is a second‑generation somatostatin receptor ligand approved for patients with acromegaly resistant/intolerant to first‑generation analogues or combination medical therapy. Real‑world evidence on its metabolic impact and tumour response remains limited. To evaluate the long‑term efficacy, metabolic safety, and tumour effects of PAS‑LAR in a real‑life cohort of acromegalic patients. This was a single-centre, retrospective observational study conducted at a tertiary endocrine centre in Romania. Thirty acromegalic patients previously treated with first-generation somatostatin receptor ligands (fg-SRLs) ± pegvisomant ± cabergoline were switched to PAS-LAR ± cabergoline. Data were collected at baseline, after 3- and 6-months of PAS-LAR treatment, and at the last available visit (median 36.5 months). Thirty patients (66.7% female; mean age 44.4 ± 12.0 years) were treated with PAS-LAR for a mean duration of 44.4 ± 31.2 months. IGF-1 xULN decreased from 1.64 ± 0.79 at baseline to 0.99 ± 0.44 at the last visit (p < 0.0001), with strict disease control (IGF-1 xULN ≤ 1.0) achieved in 60.0% of patients. Acceptable biochemical control (IGF-1 < 1.3 xULN) increased from 26.7% to 76.7% (p < 0.001). Random GH decreased from 4.26 ± 5.38 to 1.58 ± 1.43 ng/mL (p < 0.001). Median HbA1c increased from 5.65% (IQR 5.50-5.90) to 6.20% (IQR 6.03-6.88; p < 0.001). New-onset diabetes occurred in 9/24 (37.5%) patients without diabetes at baseline. At the last evaluation, HbA1c was ≥ 7.0% in 6 patients (20.0%). In exploratory analyses, higher diagnostic IGF-1 xULN correlated with greater increases in FPG (rho = 0.562, p = 0.001) and HbA1c (rho = 0.555, p = 0.001). Exploratory analyses suggested that higher IGF-1 levels at diagnosis may be associated with greater glycemic deterioration during follow-up. This potential association requires confirmation in larger cohorts. Hyperglycemic events are frequent but largely manageable with standard antidiabetic therapy. Lipid parameters remain stable or improve slightly. Early glucose monitoring should be standard during PAS‑LAR therapy.

candidates.title: Clinical and Pathological Features of Patients with Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia Type 1: A Long-Term Comparative Analysis Between Exon 2 and Other Mutations in the MEN1 Gene.
candidates.abstract: Background: Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 (MEN1) is a rare inherited syndrome characterized by primary hyperparathyroidism (PHPT), duodenopancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (DP-NET), pituitary NET (Pit-NET) and other endocrine neoplasms. Reliable genotype-phenotype correlations remain limited, and the clinical relevance of MEN1 exon 2 variants is still uncertain. Methods and aim: This monocentric retrospective cohort included genetically confirmed MEN1 patients followed at the University of Naples Federico II from January 1992 to April 2025. Eligible patients carried a pathogenic MEN-1 variant involving a single exon and had at least 36 months of follow-up. Clinical, biochemical, radiological, histopathological, genetic, and treatment data were reviewed to compare patients carrying exon 2 variants (Ex2) with those carrying variants in other exons (OtherEx) in order to evaluate mean age at diagnosis (TD) and aggressiveness of MEN-1 manifestations in these two groups. Results: Sixty patients were included: 21 Ex2 and 39 OtherEx. Follow-up was comparable between groups (133 +/- 47.7 vs. 128 +/- 50.0 months). PHPT, Pit-NET, and DP-NET had similar prevalence. DP-NET metastases were more frequent in Ex2 than OtherEx patients (4/21, 19.0% vs. 1/39, 2.6%; OR 8.94, 95% CI 0.93-86.09; p = 0.0465). When the analysis was restricted to patients who developed DP-NET, metastatic disease occurred in 4/16 Ex2 patients (25.0%) and 1/30 OtherEx patients (3.3%; OR 9.67, 95% CI 0.98-95.68; p = 0.0430). Mean DP-NET progression-free survival was numerically shorter in Ex2 patients, without statistical significance (99.6 vs. 121.6 months; p = 0.27), and DP-NET-related deaths occurred only in the Ex2 group. Additional exploratory signals included male-specific adrenal adenomas among Ex2 patients and exon 7-related bone impairment. Conclusions: This long-term MEN1 cohort suggests that exon 2 variants may identify patients with similar DP-NET prevalence but greater metastatic propensity. Because of the number of metastatic events, these findings require validation in larger multicenter cohorts.

candidates.title: Adrenal vein thrombosis during pregnancy or the postpartum period: a systematic review.
candidates.abstract: Adrenal vein thrombosis (AVT) is a rare but potentially life-threatening condition that may present as nonspecific abdominal or lower back pain during pregnancy and may be overlooked because of overlapping obstetric or gastrointestinal symptoms. AVT remains poorly characterized epidemiologically, and its management is not supported by robust evidence or consensus-based recommendations. To improve diagnosis and management, we searched the MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, ScienceDirect and Cochrane Library databases up until October 2025 for publications on AVT in pregnancy and postpartum. Thirty-eight articles reporting 73 AVT episodes in 71 patients (three retrospective studies, five case series and thirty case reports) were reviewed. Presentation was consistent but nonspecific: mainly acute abdominal (74.4%) or lower back pain (49.3%), often associated with nausea (23.3%) and vomiting (31.5%). Events occurred predominantly in the third trimester (79.6%), at a mean ± standard deviation gestational age of 31±5.7 weeks. Most cases were unilateral (63/72, 87.5%) and right-sided (48/72, 66.7%). Diagnosis relied mainly on contrast-enhanced abdominal computed tomography (56/73, 76.7%). Imaging evidenced adrenal necrosis and hemorrhage in 88.9% and 8.3% of cases, respectively. Adrenal insufficiency requiring hydrocortisone occurred in 17.1% of cases and was mainly associated with bilateral AVT. Low-molecular-weight heparin was the preferred anticoagulant during the acute phase (81.8%), followed by a switch to an oral anticoagulant postpartum (25.7%). The median treatment duration was of 24 weeks. Opioids analgesics were required in 54.8% of cases. This review summarizes the clinical presentation, diagnostic findings, management, and outcomes of AVT during pregnancy and postpartum.
candidates.journal: Journal of thrombosis and haemostasis : JTH

candidates.title: Adrenal Tumors in a Tertiary Referral Center: Clinical Insights from a Six-Year Retrospective Cohort.
candidates.abstract: Background/Objectives: Detection of adrenal tumors is increasing, mainly due to the widespread use and improved availability of radiological imaging. Their occurrence increases with age, and recent studies have reported a substantial increase in detection rates over the past few decades. This study aimed to describe the clinical spectrum and management of adrenal tumors in a real-world tertiary referral setting. Methods: This retrospective observational study was conducted to characterize the clinical presentation, diagnostic evaluation, management, and pathological spectrum of adrenal tumors treated at the University Clinical Center of Vojvodina between January 2020 and December 2025. This study included 862 patients with adrenal tumors from the outpatient clinic, day hospital, and hospital ward of the Clinic for Endocrinology, Diabetes, and Metabolic Disorders, University Clinical Center of Vojvodina, from January 2020 to December 2025. Results: Mean age was 60.73 ± 11.51 (range 19-90) years. Peak prevalence was observed in the seventh decade of life. Accordingly, 86.5% of tumors were smaller than 4 cm, 50.3% of tumors were detected in the left adrenal gland, and 14.4% were bilateral. Non-functioning tumors accounted for 85.3% of cases, while tumors showing biochemical cortisol autonomy, aldosterone-secreting tumors, and catecholamine-secreting tumors accounted for 5.7%, 4.4%, and 4.6%, respectively. CT-based assessment of tumors showed that 88.6% were adenomas, while 3.2% were cases of pheochromocytoma, 2.6% metastasis, 2.1% carcinoma, and, in smaller percentages, cysts, myelolipoma, macro- and micronodular hyperplasia, and other types. Tumor histopathology (n = 121) showed adenoma, pheochromocytoma, and metastasis as the most common (45.5%, 24%, and 10.7%, respectively). Patients with malignant lesions were significantly older than those with benign lesions (p < 0.01) and pheochromocytoma (p < 0.01). In the subgroup with histopathological diagnosis (n = 121), histopathology was significantly associated with tumor size (χ2(4) = 19.80, p < 0.001), which may reflect selection for surgery or biopsy. The mean age of patients with benign tumors, pheochromocytoma, and malignant tumors was 52.34 ± 13.86, 51.07 ± 12.35, and 63.73 ± 12.38, respectively. In the tissue-diagnosed subgroup, right-sided localization was more frequent among malignant tumors (p = 0.035), although the small number of cases warrants cautious interpretation. Conclusions: In our cohort, most adrenal tumors were benign and non-functioning, while hormonally active and malignant lesions represented a smaller but clinically important proportion requiring specialized evaluation and management. These findings provide real-world insights into adrenal tumor care in a tertiary referral setting and support the need for standardized data collection and prospective multicenter studies.

candidates.title: Meloxicam injection for the management of moderate-to-severe pain in adults.
candidates.abstract: Post-operative pain remains a significant clinical challenge, with approximately 75% of surgical patients experiencing moderate-to-severe pain. Multimodal analgesia, which combines agents targeting different pain pathways, has become the standard of care to optimize pain control while minimizing opioid-related side effects. Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) are central to this approach; however, effective intravenous options have been limited. Intravenous (IV) meloxicam, a nanocrystal formulation of the preferential COX-2 inhibitor meloxicam, has been approved by the FDA as a 30 mg, once-daily injection for moderate-to-severe pain in adults. This narrative review examines the pharmacology, pharmacokinetics, clinical efficacy, and safety of IV meloxicam in phase II and III trials across dental, gynecologic, and orthopedic surgical models. IV meloxicam may represent a promising addition to multimodal post-operative analgesia, offering rapid onset, once-daily dosing, and opioid sparing benefits. As a preferential COX-2 inhibitor, IV meloxicam may offer a more favorable safety profile compared to other nonselective NSAIDs. Additionally, IV meloxicam may possibly find a role within opioid-minimizing and enhanced recovery strategies. However, any such role will need to be confirmed by head-to-head trials against established injectable analgesics and by dedicated studies in patients with renal and hepatic impairment.

candidates.title: Recovery of adrenal function following sequential spontaneous bilateral adrenal hemorrhage.
candidates.abstract: Adrenal hemorrhage is uncommon; bilateral involvement is even rarer and can result in adrenal crisis. A 55-year-old man presented with severe atraumatic flank and low back pain; computed tomography of the abdomen revealed acute left adrenal hemorrhage. He was managed conservatively. Seven days after initial presentation, he returned with contralateral flank pain; repeat imaging demonstrated a new right adrenal hemorrhage with persistent left hemorrhage. He developed nausea, vomiting, headache, and hyponatremia; the morning cortisol was 8.99 µg/dL (248 nmol/L; reference range, 5-25 µg/dL [138-690 nmol/L]). He was admitted to the intensive care unit and treated with stress-dose hydrocortisone. Fludrocortisone was initiated as plasma renin activity was elevated. Extensive evaluation for an underlying etiology for adrenal hemorrhage was unrevealing. Serial imaging showed near-complete resolution of hematomas. Follow-up testing approximately a year after initial presentation demonstrated complete recovery of the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis, allowing for discontinuation of hydrocortisone and fludrocortisone. This case highlights the need for repeat imaging and close biochemical monitoring for adrenal insufficiency and HPA axis recovery following bilateral adrenal hemorrhage.

candidates.title: The hidden impact of laxatives on drug absorption and efficacy: a clinical perspective.
candidates.abstract: Laxatives are among the most widely used pharmacological agents worldwide, taken both as prescribed therapy and as unsupervised over-the-counter self-medication. Despite this near-ubiquitous exposure, their capacity to alter the pharmacokinetics and, consequently, the clinical efficacy or safety of concomitantly administered drugs remains under-recognized in routine practice. This article reviews under a clinical perspective the principal mechanisms by which laxatives interfere with drug absorption -accelerated intestinal transit, luminal dilution by osmotic agents, mucosal permeability changes induced by stimulant and anthranoid compounds, and electrolyte-mediated pharmacodynamic amplification- and summarizes the clinical evidence available for narrow-therapeutic-index drugs. Populations at particular risk, including patients with inflammatory bowel disease, older adults on polypharmacy, and individuals with chronic or covert laxative use, are discussed. Practical recommendations are proposed for clinicians, and priority areas for future pharmacokinetic research are outlined. The literature was identified through a search of Medline and Science Citation Index databases, supplemented by screening of relevant reference lists and clinical-trial information. The use of laxatives may interfere with the absorption of several drugs, but the literature data on this issue are still relatively scarce. The simultaneous prescription of laxatives when other drugs are used must be always carefully evaluated, especially in older subjects.
candidates.journal: Expert opinion on drug metabolism & toxicology

candidates.title: Case report: Glycemic instability despite fasting C-peptide recovery during sequential somatostatin receptor ligand therapy in acromegaly with diabetes.
candidates.abstract: Somatostatin receptor ligands (SRLs) may improve glucose metabolism by reducing growth hormone excess, but they can also suppress insulin secretion. Severe hyperglycemia is well recognized with pasireotide. Less is known about glycemic stability after recovery from severe decompensation and during later changes in SRL therapy. A 32-year-old woman with diabetes had persistent acromegaly despite transsphenoidal surgery, Gamma Knife radiosurgery, cabergoline, octreotide, and lanreotide. Pasireotide long-acting release 40 mg lowered growth hormone and insulin-like growth factor 1, but approximately 1 month later was followed by diabetic ketoacidosis and a fasting C-peptide of 0.38 ng/mL. Pasireotide was stopped, insulin-based treatment was given, and octreotide was resumed. Fasting C-peptide increased to 3.09 ng/mL within 2 months. During lanreotide re-exposure in 2025, HbA1c was 9.3% despite fasting C-peptide within the reference interval and no parallel deterioration in biochemical disease control. After lanreotide withdrawal and adjustment of diabetes therapy, intermittent hyperglycemia continued, although HbA1c decreased to 6.3% by July 2026. Return of fasting C-peptide into the reference interval after pasireotide-associated diabetic ketoacidosis did not predict sustained glycemic stability in this patient. The later deterioration during lanreotide therapy was temporally associated with treatment but does not establish causality. The overall course is more consistent with persistent metabolic vulnerability despite normalization of fasting C-peptide than with confirmed recurrent SRL-induced dysglycemia. Glucose monitoring should be intensified when an SRL is started or changed in patients with diabetes or previous ketosis.

candidates.title: Diagnostic and Translational Challenges in Canine Endocrine and Neuroendocrine Neoplasms: A Comparative Pathology Perspective.
candidates.abstract: The recognition and detection of endocrine and neuroendocrine neoplasms (NENs) in dogs and humans is challenging. This is, in part, because some are non-functional, and where hormone hypersecretion occurs, it can lead to a great variety of clinical syndromes. Additionally, metastatic patterns vary according to the primary anatomical site, and the typically slow growth of many endocrine tumours/NENs may lead to underestimation of biological aggressiveness and misclassification as benign disease. In human medicine, diagnostic evaluation relies on a comprehensive, anatomical site-specific histopathologic framework, incorporating immunohistochemistry as formalised in the 2025 World Health Organisation classification of endocrine tumours/NENs. In contrast, veterinary diagnostic frameworks for canine endocrine tumours/NENs remain comparatively underdeveloped, with limited standardisation of terminology, grading systems, and validated cut-off values. This review aims to raise awareness of key diagnostic challenges associated with the most clinically prevalent canine endocrine tumours/NENs: insulinoma, phaeochromocytoma and cortisol-producing adrenocortical tumours. Emphasis is placed on histopathological characterisation using immunohistochemistry, drawing parallels with established human diagnostic algorithms where appropriate. By synthesising current knowledge from human and canine pathology, this review highlights critical gaps in veterinary diagnostic practice and identifies opportunities for harmonisation of classification strategies. The development of standardised diagnostic guidelines has the potential not only to improve clinical management of affected dogs but also to strengthen the translational value of spontaneous canine endocrine tumours/NENs within the field of comparative oncology and One Medicine.

candidates.title: Reconstruction with a novel pedicled mucoperiosteal hinge flap and dura suturing: a new minimally invasive concept and closure technique for endoscopic endonasal surgery.
candidates.abstract: The authors aimed to evaluate their experience with the minimally invasive reconstruction technique using pedicled mucoperiostea hinge flap (PMHF) with dura suturing after EES. Outcomes were compared with those of the traditional reconstruction using the NSF. The authors conducted a retrospective cohort study involving 33 consecutive patients who underwent EES for pituitary adenoma resection. All these 33 patients were reconstructed with pedicled mucoperiosteal hinge flap with dura suturing and were compared with 32 consecutive patients treated previously using NSF technique. Surgical videos and electronic medical records were reviewed to assess operative times and postoperative outcomes, which were compared between the groups, with a particular focus on nasal function, assessed using the Endoscopic Endonasal Sinus and Skull Base Surgery Questionnaire (EES-Q). Demographics of the two groups were broadly similar. Among the 33 patients using PMHF with dura suturing, the average operative time decreased with experience, showing a trend of improved efficiency. No significant difference was observed between two groups in terms of total operative time. One postoperative CSF leak (3%) was observed in PMHF group, while 2 postoperative CSF leak (6%) occurred in group using NSF (P = 0.61). Importantly, patients who underwent reconstruction with pedicled mucoperiosteal hinge flap with dura suturing reported significantly lower EES-Q scores overall (p < 0.01), with better outcomes in all domains (p < 0.01). This technique provides a reliable method for preventing postoperative CSF leak and a less invasive option, ultimately contributing to the preservation of the patient's quality of life (QOL).

candidates.title: Bilateral adrenal diffuse large B-cell lymphoma masquerading as bilateral adrenal metastases: a rare presentation diagnosed by endoscopic ultrasound-guided fine-needle biopsy.
candidates.abstract: Bilateral adrenal diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) is an exceedingly rare entity. Presentation as bilateral adrenal masses without an identifiable extra-adrenal primary poses a formidable diagnostic challenge, frequently mimicking adrenal metastases or primary adrenal malignancy. A 70-year-old normotensive, non-diabetic male presented with a one-month history of weight loss, generalized dull abdominal pain, and anorexia. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CECT) revealed bilateral adrenal masses (right 56 × 28 × 55 mm; left 61 × 30 × 54 mm) with imaging characteristics indistinguishable from metastatic disease. Extensive workup-including CT of the neck and chest, colonoscopy, and biochemical adrenal profiling-failed to identify a primary extra-adrenal malignancy or hormonal excess. Endoscopic ultrasound-guided fine-needle biopsy (EUS-FNB) using a 22-gauge needle provided tissue confirming diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) with CD20 and PAX-5 positivity. The patient was referred to oncology and commenced on rituximab-based chemotherapy. This case underscores the indispensable role of EUS-guided tissue sampling in the evaluation of bilateral adrenal masses when non-invasive workup is inconclusive. Early tissue diagnosis of adrenal DLBCL is critical, as it is a potentially curable disease amenable to immunochemotherapy rather than surgery.

candidates.title: Detection of Salmonella Typhi, associated microbial communities and AMR genes within wastewater in Harare, Zimbabwe.
candidates.abstract: Water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) infrastructure is critical to the control of transmission of bacterial pathogens, such as Salmonella enterica serotype Typhi (S. Typhi). Wastewater harbours a complex microbial community of bacteria that encode antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) capable of transfer to bacterial pathogens and protists which have the potential to provide an intracellular niche contributing to pathogen transmission. Here, we report the microbial communities and resistome within wastewater treatment plants in Harare, Zimbabwe, where typhoid fever is endemic. The detection of S. Typhi using metagenome sequence and quantitative PCR (qPCR) was investigated. A total of 3,239 miTag groups of bacteria from 58 classified phyla were detected, with Pseudomonadota as the dominant taxon. Salmonella detection in metagenome sequence lacked sensitivity and specificity. Instead, qPCR using primers that can discriminate between Salmonella serotypes detects these pathogens at high prevalence in wastewater. The protist community was diverse, comprising 576 taxa, including phyla, such as Bigyra and Fornicata. We detected a difference in protist community diversity in influent or effluent samples. A significant reduction in metagenome sequences that mapped to ARGs was observed in effluent compared to influent samples, including a 1,000-fold decrease in ARGs conferring resistance to quinolone antibiotics, a class important as a first-line treatment for typhoid fever. Our data highlight the importance of WASH infrastructure to decrease the opportunity for interaction between protists and bacterial pathogens, the transfer of ARGs and transmission to the public.

candidates.title: Benefits of Intracystic Bleomycin for Symptomatic Recurrent Rathke Cleft Cyst: An Institutional Update.
candidates.abstract: The management of recurrent Rathke cleft cysts (RCC) poses a unique clinical challenge. The mainstay of treatment is reoperation with cyst drainage; however, there is limited evidence evaluating adjuvant pharmaceutical therapy in this patient population. Several studies, including a 2019 study by Ung et al at our institution, suggest a potential benefit of the use of intracystic bleomycin in recurrent RCC. The intracystic application of bleomycin is known to be beneficial in the treatment of cystic craniopharyngioma, however, its role in the treatment of recurrent Rathke cleft cyst remains unclear. To evaluate long-term outcomes of recurrent RCC treated with intracystic bleomycin, building on a 2019 study by our institution which reported no short-term follow-up recurrence. We conducted a retrospective chart review of patients with RCC who underwent surgical resection with intracystic bleomycin between January 2011 and December 2023 by a single surgeon. This study updates our 2019 study which reported no recurrence in 6 patients who received intracystic bleomycin for recurrent RCC. Patient symptom ratings were collected preoperatively and postoperatively. Of 125 patients with a history of surgery for RCC, 29 (23%) experienced radiographic recurrence. Subsequently, 24 of these patients underwent reresection with 20 of these patients receiving intracystic bleomycin at the time of secondary resection. To date, only 2 bleomycin-treated patients experienced recurrence (10%) with a median follow-up of 28.4 [4.0-54.4] months. Compared with historical data which show a 26.2% recurrence rate after secondary resection without adjuvant therapy, our bleomycin-treated cohort demonstrated a lower recurrence rate. The use of intracystic bleomycin seems to be a safe and potentially effective treatment option in patients with recurrent RCC.

candidates.title: Patients with acromegaly who underwent surgery at Haukeland University Hospital, 2015-2024.
candidates.abstract: Acromegaly is a rare disease. The aim of this study was to describe the clinical characteristics, course of treatment and outcomes of patients who underwent surgery for acromegaly at Haukeland University Hospital in the period 2015-2024. A retrospective review of medical records of patients who underwent surgery for acromegaly between 1. January 2015 and 31 December 2024. A total of 23 patients were included in the study, 11 of whom were women (48 %). The median age at diagnosis was 60 years (range 26-81). Macroadenomas were identified in 17 patients (74 %). Six patients (26 %) were in remission at the 3-month follow-up after primary surgery. At the last follow-up, after a median of 70 months (range 7-126), nine patients (39 %) were in remission. Fourteen patients received further treatment in the form of pharmacotherapy, repeat surgery and/or radiotherapy. Acromegaly is a rare disease, and the high proportion of macroadenomas suggests late diagnosis. Many patients do not achieve remission after surgery and require further treatment to control the disease.
candidates.journal: Tidsskrift for den Norske laegeforening : tidsskrift for praktisk medicin, ny raekke

candidates.title: Life-Threatening Retroperitoneal Hematoma After Radial PCI: A Rare Case of Spontaneous Lumbar Artery Bleeding.
candidates.abstract: Spontaneous retroperitoneal hematoma is a rare, life-threatening complication of antithrombotic therapy, seldom considered after radial percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). A 71-year-old man underwent radial PCI of the right coronary artery 3 days after streptokinase for inferior myocardial infarction on dual antiplatelet therapy and enoxaparin. Twelve hours later, he developed abdominal pain and hypotension, with hemoglobin falling from 11.6 to 6 g/dL. Computed tomography showed a large left retroperitoneal hematoma with active extravasation, and angiography localized bleeding to the left third lumbar artery, which was successfully embolized. Recovery was complicated by acute renal failure requiring dialysis; the hematoma resolved on follow-up. Layered fibrinolytic, antiplatelet, and anticoagulant exposure can cause spontaneous non-access-site bleeding even after radial access, where retroperitoneal hemorrhage is rarely suspected. Radial access does not eliminate major bleeding risk. Unexplained hypotension after PCI should prompt early imaging to exclude retroperitoneal hemorrhage.

candidates.title: Efficacy of radionuclide therapy in the treatment of inoperable or metastatic pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma.
candidates.abstract: Inoperable or metastatic pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma (PC/PGL) present a management challenge with high variability in response to systemic therapies. The aim of this study was to assess the efficacy and toxicity of 2 therapeutic radiopharmaceutical agents: iodine-131 metaiodobenzylguanine and lutetium-177 DOTA-octreotate. This retrospective audit assessed the efficacy of radionuclide therapy in the treatment of progressive inoperable or metastatic PC/PGL utilizing 3 variables to assess response: clinical (symptomatic and antihypertensive medication dose changes); hormonal (catecholamine or plasma metanephrine levels); and radiological (tumor size). Response was assessed at the first clinical review following initial treatment. For patients receiving more than a single dose of radionuclide therapy, longitudinal data on additional therapies, treatment response, and survival analysis was performed. 16 treatment-naïve patients were included in this study: 9 patients were diagnosed with PC and 7 with PGL. Eight patients received iodine-131 metaiodobenzylguanine and 8 lutetium-177 DOTA-octreotate. There was a significant fall in the mean systolic blood pressure following administration of radionuclide therapy: 133 mmHg [IQR 124.5-145.5] to 127 mmHg [IQR 112.5-130.8] (P = .05). Disease control rate was high for all variables (clinical 92%; hormonal 100%; radiological 100%). Overall response rate was greatest clinically (clinical 83%; hormonal 45%; radiological 8%). Median progression-free survival (PFS; defined as progression in clinical, hormonal, or radiological variables) was 17 months (95% CI, 9-27). Specific to radiological progression, that is PC/PGL tumor progression as determined by RECIST 1.1, the PFS was 53 months (95% CI, 27-62). The median overall survival was not reached in this cohort. Patients diagnosed with progressive inoperable or metastatic PC/PGLs have few therapeutic options. We have shown the efficacy of iodine-131 metaiodobenzylguanine and lutetium-177 DOTA-octreotate with improvement of symptoms associated with catecholamine excess, blood pressure control, and hormone secretion, as well as stabilization of tumor growth.

candidates.title: Anesthetic challenges and management strategies in patients with prior chimeric antigen receptor T-cell exposure, immunotherapy and thoracic noncardiac anesthesia.
candidates.abstract: The increasing use of immunotherapy and targeted cancer therapies has added an additional layer of complexity to the management of thoracic malignancies. This review summarizes contemporary systemic cancer therapies and their treatment-related toxicities relevant to the anesthetic management of patients undergoing thoracic noncardiac surgery. Immune checkpoint inhibitors and chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapies cause multi-organ toxicities across pulmonary, cardiovascular, endocrine, neurological, hematological, and renal systems. Checkpoint inhibitor pneumonitis, myocarditis, adrenal insufficiency, and neurological syndromes can persist beyond treatment, impacting perioperative care. CAR T-cell therapies carry risks of cytokine release syndrome, immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome, coagulopathies, prolonged cytopenias, and cardiopulmonary complications. Combined with the stress of thoracic surgery and one-lung ventilation, these toxicities require an individualized, multidisciplinary approach. Emerging modalities, including cancer vaccines and oncolytic viruses, present additional novel considerations. Safe perioperative care requires understanding treatment-specific toxicities, comprehensive preoperative assessment, individualized ventilation and hemodynamic strategies, structured postoperative management, and essential multidisciplinary collaboration as therapies evolve.

candidates.title: Variable Expressivity of von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) Disease Associated with c.499C>T Variant in a Multigenerational Family.
candidates.abstract: von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) disease is an autosomal dominant cancer syndrome caused by germline pathogenic variants in the VHL tumor suppressor gene manifesting as a spectrum of neoplasms, including the central nervous system (CNS) and retinal hemangioblastomas, pheochromocytoma, renal cell carcinoma (RCC), pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (PNETs), and paraganglioma. This study systematically evaluates the clinical, radiological, and molecular genetic profiles of a large multigeneration family harboring the pathogenic variant c.499C>T (p.Arg167Trp). Affected individuals and at-risk family members underwent clinical exome sequencing and targeted cascade molecular testing. Variants were classified according to the 2015 guidelines of the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics-Association for Molecular Pathology. Multidisciplinary follow-up encompassed neurological, endocrinological, ophthalmological, and radiological evaluations, including optical coherence tomography and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) surveillance. Among 47 individuals tested across five generations, 23 were confirmed to carry the heterozygous pathogenic variant c.499C>T (p.Arg167Trp) in the VHL gene (NM_000551.4). Among the 23 molecularly confirmed carriers (which included several young carriers still under surveillance), pheochromocytoma was the most prevalent manifestation (5/23), followed by CNS hemangioblastoma (3/23), retinal angioma (2/23), PNET (2/23), and pancreatic cysts (2/23). No RCC was identified among molecularly confirmed carriers. Clinical presentations were consistent with multiple VHL disease subtypes, reflecting broad intrafamilial phenotypic heterogeneity. The c.499C>T (p.Arg167Trp) variant demonstrates remarkable phenotypic variability, ranging from multiple concurrent VHL-associated neoplasms to asymptomatic carrier status within the same family. These findings underscore the necessity of lifelong multidisciplinary surveillance and comprehensive cascade genetic testing in the clinical management of VHL disease.
candidates.journal: Journal of kidney cancer and VHL

candidates.title: Papillary craniopharyngioma mistaken for recurrent Rathke's cleft cyst: a case report of a seven-year diagnostic pitfall involving BRAF V600E testing.
candidates.abstract: Rathke's cleft cysts (RCC) and craniopharyngiomas are clinically, radiologically and histopathologically similar lesions that are difficult to distinguish and require different surgical treatments. Many authors support the hypothesis that these represent two spectra of the same pathology. We present the case of a 53-year-old man who, because of general malaise, was examined by an endocrinologist and found to have partial hypopituitarism and indirect hyperprolactinemia. Consequently, he underwent a head MRI, which revealed an intra-suprasellar cystic lesion. Surgical fenestration of the cyst was performed, and tissue samples were collected for histopathological examination, which confirmed a diagnosis of RCC. Over the years, follow-up imaging revealed a recurrent, enlarging cyst; therefore, the patient underwent reoperation 7.5 years later. This time, histology revealed a papillary craniopharyngioma (PC). Re-examination of the specimen from the first surgery also confirmed presence of PC on the same specimen section as RCC, with the initial false-negative result attributed to suboptimal staining. Apparent progression from RCC to craniopharyngioma should prompt re-examination of the original pathology before it is interpreted as true transformation. In our patient, conservative fenestration was followed by recovery of corticotroph function that lasted seven years, whereas subsequent radical surgery resulted in new corticotroph and thyrotroph deficiency without complete resection, highlighting the need for caution with early aggressive surgery in cystic sellar lesions of uncertain histology.
